why: “In your Command phase … you can select one protocol … Once a unit enters a protocol, it remains in that protocol until it enters a different one”: a different protocol can only be entered in your Command phase, so the effect surely lasts until the start of your next Command phase, which is 'round'. That carries Protector’s +2 A into every later step of this turn and the opponent’s, and no longer than the words. The rest of the footnote is unchanged.

Same words as the Protector footnote: “it remains in that protocol until it enters a different one”, and a new one is selected only “In your Command phase”. So Conqueror’s +2 A to the Twin Kastelan fist is sure to last until the start of your next Command phase, which is 'round', and no longer. The rest of the footnote is unchanged.

It now uses the rule’s words: “a unit that is not fully visible to the attacking model because of one or more models in your SMOKE unit … the target has the benefit of cover against that attack (13.08)”. “to the attacking models” fits the calculator’s cover tick, which counts for all of a step’s attacks, and 13.08 decides cover per attacking model. The box it names exists with that label (app.html: 'Target has the benefit of cover').
